plan.text: Add an SGLT2 inhibitor for chronic kidney disease, independent of HbA1c (eGFR 54.9); give sick-day guidance to pause it during dehydrating illness.

summary_text:
58-year-old man with hypertension and diabetes, current smoker. Today: BP 160/97 mmHg, HbA1c 9.2%, eGFR 54.9, ACR 12 mg/mmol, LDL 3.4 mmol/L, BMI 31.1. 3 current medicines.

Impression: Priorities: 1) Hypertension (uncontrolled); 2) Diabetes (above target); 3) Cardiovascular risk and lipids (untreated); 4) Reduced kidney function or albuminuria G3aA2 (needs confirmation).

1. Hypertension [uncontrolled]
   Above target at 160/97 mmHg (target <130/80 mmHg); systolic 30 mmHg above the systolic goal on 1 antihypertensive class.
   Target: <130/80 mmHg (WHO 2021 systolic <130 with CVD, diabetes, CKD or high risk)
   - Confirm with correctly measured seated readings and, where available, home or ambulatory BP to exclude a white-coat effect before escalating.
   - Add an ACE inhibitor or ARB as the second class (also indicated for albuminuria; see kidney plan) rather than only up-titrating monotherapy.
   - Lifestyle: salt below 5 g/day, regular physical activity, limit alcohol, and weight reduction (BMI 31.1).

2. Diabetes [above target]
   HbA1c 9.2% is 2.2 points above the individual target of <7.0% on metformin.
   Target: HbA1c <7.0% (53 mmol/mol) for most adults without hypoglycaemia
   - Add an SGLT2 inhibitor for chronic kidney disease, independent of HbA1c (eGFR 54.9); give sick-day guidance to pause it during dehydrating illness.
   - If HbA1c remains above target after the SGLT2 inhibitor (expected fall about 0.5%), add an agent chosen by comorbidity, cost and hypoglycaemia risk: a GLP-1 receptor agonist (weight benefit; BMI 31.1); a sulfonylurea where cost limits access (gliclazide preferred; avoid glibenclamide from age 60); a DPP-4 inhibitor (low hypoglycaemia risk); basal insulin.
   - Retinal screening is overdue: arrange dilated eye examination or retinal photography.
   - Foot examination is not documented: check sensation (10 g monofilament), pulses and skin; educate on daily foot care.

3. Cardiovascular risk and lipids [untreated]
   Very high cardiovascular risk (diabetes with kidney target-organ damage). LDL goal <1.4 mmol/L.
   Target: LDL <1.4 mmol/L and ≥50% reduction from baseline
   - Start a high-intensity statin (atorvastatin 40–80 mg or rosuvastatin 20–40 mg class): indicated for diabetes at age 58.

4. Reduced kidney function or albuminuria G3aA2 [needs confirmation]
   KDIGO risk category high.
   Target: Systolic BP <120 mmHg with standardised measurement if tolerated (KDIGO), otherwise <130/80
   - Confirm chronicity: repeat eGFR and urine ACR after 3 months and exclude acute kidney injury (compare with previous results).
   - Start an ACE inhibitor or ARB titrated to the maximum tolerated dose for albuminuria (ACR 12 mg/mmol); recheck creatinine and potassium in 2–4 weeks and accept a creatinine rise of up to 30%.
   - Stop NSAIDs and avoid other nephrotoxins; adjust renally cleared medicines to eGFR.
   - Give sick-day guidance: pause metformin, SGLT2 inhibitors, ACE inhibitor/ARB and diuretics during vomiting, diarrhoea or poor intake, and restart when eating and drinking.

5. Obesity [at risk]
   Weight contributes to BP, glucose and cardiovascular risk.
   - Agree a 5–10% weight-loss goal with diet, activity and follow-up support.
   - In diabetes, a GLP-1 receptor agonist supports both glucose and weight goals where available.

6. Current tobacco use [at risk]
   Stopping is the single most effective intervention for cardiovascular and lung risk.
   - Give brief advice to quit today and offer behavioural support with pharmacotherapy (varenicline, nicotine replacement, bupropion or cytisine) where available; follow up within 2 weeks.

Medication review:
   - NSAID (ibuprofen) with kidney disease and raised BP: Avoid NSAIDs; use paracetamol or topical agents and review over-the-counter use.

Monitoring:
   - Blood pressure: Every 2–4 weeks after each change until at target, then every 3–6 months
   - Vitamin B12: Periodically on long-term metformin, especially with neuropathy or anaemia
   - HbA1c: Every 3 months until at target, then every 6 months
   - eGFR and urine ACR: 2 times per year (G3aA2)
   - Lipid profile: 4–12 weeks after starting or changing a statin, then annually

Follow-up: 2–4 weeks: confirm readings, review changes and blood results.
Decision support for clinician review; not a prescription.
